(1) we propose a technique for assessing the effectiveness of adversarial attacks and defenses; (2) we use our technique to demonstrate that the recently proposed attack technique is significantly stronger than the state-of-the-art attack techniques; and (3) we use our techniques to show that the recently proposed defense technique is not effective.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of the art in adversarial examples is still far from satisfactory.
the current state of the art in adversarial attacks is still far from perfect and that we still do not have a good understanding of the robustness of deep learning algorithms to adversarial attacks.
the current defense techniques are not effective, and the current attack techniques are effective, but not as effective as the ground truths.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach for constructing ground truths, and used it to assess the robustness of networks against adversarial examples.
the current state of adversarial robustness is far from being satisfactory.
we propose to construct ground truths: provably-minimal adversarial examples, and demonstrate how they could be used to assess attack and defense techniques.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to assess a defense technique's effectiveness, it is necessary to use an attack technique that is stronger than the one the defense was designed against.
ground truths are a valuable tool in evaluating defenses, and can help in the design of more effective defenses.
, while existing attacks are effective in practice, the ground-truth adversarial examples that we construct are significantly more effective in practice.
